o: Medial femoral circumflex artery (deep branch) → retinacular vessels

en.q: Poor reduction of pubic ramus during ilioinguinal can endanger:
The "falx inguinalis" (conjoint tendon) is:
o: Fusion of transversus abdominis + internal oblique aponeuroses

en.q: The pelvic brim (linea terminalis) runs along:
o: Sacral promontory → iliopectineal line → pubic tubercle

en.q: Meralgia paresthetica results from compression/injury of:
Which is a principal advantage of the modified Stoppa over the classic ilioinguinal approach?
o: Eliminates the need to protect the corona mortis
Better exposure of the posterior wall
Better visualization of the quadrilateral surface and medial acetabular wall

en.q: The gluteus maximus split in Kocher-Langenbeck is biased laterally to preserve innervation from:
The short external rotators from superior to inferior are:
o: Piriformis, obturator externus, gemellus inf., gemellus sup., quadratus femoris
Quadratus femoris, gemellus inf., obturator internus, gemellus sup., piriformis
Piriformis, gemellus sup., obturator internus, gemellus inf., quadratus femoris
Gluteus minimus, gemellus sup., obturator internus, piriformis, gemellus inf.

en.q: Why has the extended iliofemoral approach been largely abandoned in favor of staged approaches?
o: High heterotopic ossification rate (50-90%) and abductor dysfunction
Inability to reduce the posterior wall

en.q: Which vein is particularly vulnerable in anterior pelvic approaches because of its medial position relative to the artery?
o: Femoral vein in the adductor canal

en.q: In modified Stoppa, midline dissection of the rectus abdominis uses which avascular plane?
Kocher-Langenbeck exposure can be extended proximally to the supra-acetabular region via:
o: Trochanteric osteotomy (incl. Ganz trochanteric flip osteotomy)

en.q: Inguinal hernia frequency after the ilioinguinal approach is approximately:
Which nerve is at risk in the medial parapatellar incision?
o: Infrapatellar branch of the saphenous nerve

en.q: The interval in the posterolateral knee approach (Henderson) is:
o: Biceps femoris/iliotibial band above, lateral gastrocnemius/popliteus below

en.q: What is the Trickey incision pattern?
o: S-shaped incision over the popliteal fossa, passing lateral to popliteal vessels

en.q: The geniculate anastomosis around the knee is formed by:
o: Superior medial/lateral, inferior medial/lateral, middle, descending genicular, anterior tibial recurrent
